newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures got a boost on Wednesday amid a favourable backdrop in other bond markets and investment from non-resident investors pushing the September contract to a new high.

A slide in the French stock market, fuelled by fears of increases in corporate taxes, spilled over to bonds and knocked the contract of its peak, but most traders said they saw little logic behind the decline and prices soon stabilised.
There was little reaction to a larger-than-expected decline in U.S. May factory orders with caution the order of the day ahead of the outcome of a U.S. policy-making meeting.

Traders said while the U.S. Federal Reserve was widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged after its meeting - a statement was expected at 1815 GMT - a key June U.S. jobs report due on Thursday was also keeping investors on their guard.

Analysts said the rally in the dollar against European currencies was positive for European bonds as it could both restrain the U.S. economy, reducing the need for rate rises, and help European growth, needed to help cut public deficits.
The dollar rose to a high of 5.9095 against the franc on Wednesday, its strongest level since February 1994. The franc was steady against the mark at 3.3694.
Traders said there was a risk of some declines on Thursday ahead of the auction of a new 10-year government bond, a 5.50 percent October 25, 2007 OAT, and before the U.S. jobs data.

In the event of any slippage the gap opened at Wednesday's start between 129.42 and 129.50 would be the first area of support and in any case traders said buyers have been quick to step in on any dips.

A trader at a U.S. house said this was the case when the bond future declined in tandem with the French stock exchange on Wednesday. "People were asking if corporate taxes will hurt the bond market, for me it was a good buying opportunity," he said.

The Treasury will offer 21 to 23 billion francs of OATs at Thursday's auction with the lion's share going to the new benchmark bond and two to four billion to be allocated to the 2009 TEC 10 variable rate OAT, said to be in some demand from domestic investors.

The spread between French and German 10-year bond yields moved to minus 14 basis points early in the session as some non-residents bought French bond futures and sold Bund futures but moved back to minus 12 after the slippage with the CAC 40.
